Indicator 13 tracks a critical safety metric in cardiology: the proportion of newly diagnosed atrial fibrillation patients who experience an intracranial hemorrhage within one year [^src1]. This comparison evaluates the incidence rates across national, regional, and local health cluster levels in Denmark, providing a granular view of patient outcomes and potential bleeding risks associated with early treatment [^src1].

Nationally, [[danmark|Danmark]] reports an incidence rate of 0.8%, with 173 hemorrhage events recorded among 21,804 newly diagnosed patients [^src1]. At the regional level, [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] has the highest rate at 1.0% (48 out of 4,972 patients), while [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] records the lowest at 0.5% (11 out of 2,419) [^src1]. The remaining regions—[[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]], [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]], and [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]]—all align with the national average of 0.8% [^src1].

When examining the more granular health clusters, [[sundhedsklynge-bornholm|Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]] emerges as the leader with the highest rate at 1.5% (3 out of 195 patients) [^src1]. Other clusters with elevated rates include [[klynge-syd|Klynge SYD]] at 1.3%, alongside [[sundhedsklyngen-nykoebing-f|Sundhedsklyngen Nykøbing F]] and [[sundhedsklynge-sydvestjylland|Sundhedsklynge Sydvestjylland]], both at 1.2% [^src1]. On the opposite end, [[klynge-midt|Klynge MIDT]] is the trailer, reporting a 0.0% incidence rate with zero events among 866 patients [^src1]. [[sundhedsklynge-midt|Sundhedsklynge Midt]] follows closely with a 0.4% rate [^src1].

Regarding performance targets, the "Standard opfyldt" (Standard met) column uniformly displays "0 (0)" for every geographic entity, indicating that no specific target threshold is marked as achieved or evaluated in this reporting format [^src1]. 

Because this comparison is built from a single dated table section, no cross-sectional trend analysis can be performed across multiple report years. However, the table's internal historical columns reveal that the national rate was 0.7% in the immediate prior year and 0.8% the year before that [^src1]. 

Statistical outliers are primarily driven by denominator size. [[sundhedsklynge-bornholm|Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]]'s 1.5% rate is heavily influenced by its small patient cohort of 195, resulting in a wide 95% confidence interval of 0.3-4.4 [^src1]. Similarly, [[klynge-midt|Klynge MIDT]] stands out for dropping to zero events in the current year after recording 5 events in the previous year, highlighting the volatility of rare adverse events in smaller populations [^src1].
